sources.finding: Pooling 191 controlled studies, every type of exercise lowered resting heart rate, with endurance training and yoga the only types reducing it significantly in both men and women.

sources.citation: Rhee J, Iansavitchene A, Mannala S, Graham ME, Rotenberg B. Breaking social media fads and uncovering the safety and efficacy of mouth taping in patients with mouth breathing, sleep disordered breathing, or obstructive sleep apnea: a systematic review. PLoS One. 2025;20(5):e0323643.
sources.finding: Ten poor-quality studies, 213 patients, none testing healthy sleepers: two showed significant breathing gains in mild sleep apnea; authors flag risks with nasal blockage and do not support taping.
sources.population: adults with sleep apnea, mouth breathing or nasal obstruction

sources.citation: Riebe D, Franklin BA, Thompson PD, et al. Updating ACSM's recommendations for exercise preparticipation health screening. Med Sci Sports Exerc 47(11):2473-2479.
sources.finding: ACSM screening now rests on current activity level, known heart, metabolic or kidney disease or symptoms, and the intensity planned, dropping risk-factor counting to reduce needless barriers.

sources.citation: Rimm EB, Appel LJ, Chiuve SE, et al. Seafood long-chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and cardiovascular disease: a science advisory from the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2018;138(1):e35-e47.
sources.finding: The AHA supports one to two seafood meals a week, linked to lower risk of heart failure, coronary disease and sudden cardiac death, most when seafood replaces less healthy foods.

sources.citation: Roberts LA, Raastad T, Markworth JF, et al. Post-exercise cold water immersion attenuates acute anabolic signalling and long-term adaptations in muscle to strength training. J Physiol 593(18):4285-4301.
sources.finding: Over 12 weeks of twice-weekly lifting, men taking 10-minute cold baths after sessions gained less strength and muscle than men doing active recovery.

sources.citation: Robey E, Dawson B, Halson S, et al. Effect of evening postexercise cold water immersion on subsequent sleep. Med Sci Sports Exerc 45(7):1394-1402.
sources.finding: In 11 trained cyclists, a cold bath after evening exercise left sleep onset, total sleep and sleep stages unchanged on lab sleep tests, though core temperature stayed lower.

sources.citation: Robinson LA, Cavanah AM, Lennon S, et al. Epigenetic and microbiome responses to greens supplementation in obese older adults: results from a randomized crossover-controlled trial. Front Nutr. 2026;13:1750030.
sources.finding: BrickHouse Nutrition paid for this 30-day open-label crossover in 19 adults with obesity; Field of Greens left metabolic markers, body composition, sleep and mood unchanged.

sources.citation: Robson AR, Ellis JG, Elder GJ. Poor false sleep feedback does not affect pre-sleep cognitive arousal or subjective sleep continuity in healthy sleepers: a pilot study. Sleep Biol Rhythms. 2022;20(4):467-472.
sources.finding: In 54 healthy sleepers, a one-off fake good or poor sleep score did not change pre-sleep arousal or diary-rated sleep over the following week.

sources.citation: Rock CL, Flatt SW, Sherwood NE, et al. Effect of a free prepared meal and incentivized weight loss program on weight loss and weight loss maintenance in obese and overweight women: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA.
sources.finding: In 442 women with overweight, a structured program built on prepackaged meals produced 6 to 7 kg loss at two years, versus 2 kg with usual care.
sources.population: women aged 18 to 69 with overweight or obesity

sources.citation: Rock CL, Flatt SW, Pakiz B, et al. Randomized clinical trial of portion-controlled prepackaged foods to promote weight loss. Obesity (Silver Spring).
sources.finding: In 183 adults with overweight, adding portion-controlled frozen entrees to counselling gave 8.6% versus 6.0% weight loss at 12 weeks; Nestle, the entrees' maker, funded it.
sources.population: adults aged 25 to 65 with overweight or obesity

sources.citation: Rönsch H, Bauer A. The preventive value of sun protection. Curr Probl Dermatol. 2021;55:316-328.
sources.finding: Found five controlled trials; both photoaging trials showed less aging with sunscreen, but the authors call the overall evidence base limited and keep shade and clothing first.
sources.population: people in controlled sunscreen trials (28 to 1,621 per trial)

sources.citation: Rosman L, Lampert R, Zhuo S, et al. Wearable devices, health care use, and psychological well-being in patients with atrial fibrillation. J Am Heart Assoc. 2024;13(15):e033750.
sources.finding: In 172 patients with atrial fibrillation, wearable users reported more symptom monitoring and preoccupation and used more heart-related care than matched non-users.

sources.citation: Ross AC, Manson JE, Abrams SA, et al. The 2011 report on dietary reference intakes for calcium and vitamin D from the Institute of Medicine: what clinicians need to know. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2011;96(1):53-58.
sources.finding: 600 IU/day covers ages 1-70; a blood level of 20 ng/mL (50 nmol/L) meets bone needs for nearly everyone; non-bone benefits were inconsistent and inconclusive.

sources.citation: Ryan J, Edney S, Maher C. Anxious or empowered? A cross-sectional study exploring how wearable activity trackers make their owners feel. BMC Psychol. 2019;7(1):42.
sources.finding: Among 237 adult wearable users, wearing the device brought more positive than negative feelings, but being unable to wear it flipped this toward anxiety and frustration.

sources.citation: Salve J, Pate S, Debnath K, Langade D. Adaptogenic and anxiolytic effects of Ashwagandha root extract in healthy adults: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical study. Cureus. 2019;11(12):e6466.
sources.finding: In 58 stressed adults over 8 weeks, KSM-66 at 250 mg and 600 mg daily improved sleep quality, perceived stress and cortisol versus placebo; product supplied by its maker.

sources.citation: Sapp PA, Townsend JR, Kirby TO, et al. Absorption kinetics of vitamins and minerals from a novel nutritional product in physically active adults: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Front Nutr. 2026;13:1793264.
sources.finding: In 16 active adults, one AG1 serving raised blood levels of most measured vitamins and minerals over eight hours versus placebo. Five authors list AG1 affiliations.

sources.citation: Sateia MJ, Buysse DJ, Krystal AD, Neubauer DN, Heald JL. Clinical practice guideline for the pharmacologic treatment of chronic insomnia in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline. J Clin Sleep Med. 2017;13(2):307-349.
sources.finding: AASM guideline: weak recommendation against melatonin (2 mg prolonged-release), valerian and diphenhydramine for chronic insomnia, since measured effects fell below clinical-significance thresholds; evidence quality low to very low.

sources.citation: American College of Sports Medicine; Sawka MN, Burke LM, Eichner ER, et al. American College of Sports Medicine position stand: exercise and fluid replacement. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
sources.finding: ACSM advises individual fluid plans because sweat rates and sweat sodium vary; electrolyte-carbohydrate drinks can beat water during exercise in some circumstances.

sources.citation: Schuster J, Cycelskij I, Lopresti A, Hahn A. Magnesium bisglycinate supplementation in healthy adults reporting poor sleep: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial. Nat Sci Sleep. 2025;17:2027-2040.
sources.finding: 155 adults with self-reported poor sleep: 250 mg magnesium as bisglycinate nightly for 4 weeks lowered insomnia scores slightly more than placebo (small effect); other outcomes unchanged.
sources.population: adults 18 to 65 reporting poor sleep, Germany (mean age 41, about 80% women)

sources.citation: Scullin MK, Krueger ML, Ballard HK, Pruett N, Bliwise DL. The effects of bedtime writing on difficulty falling asleep: a polysomnographic study comparing to-do lists and completed activity lists. J Exp Psychol Gen. 2018;147(1):139-146.
sources.finding: In a one-night sleep-lab study of 57 healthy young adults, five minutes writing a specific to-do list led to faster sleep onset than writing about completed tasks.

sources.citation: Sesso HD, Rist PM, Aragaki AK, et al. Multivitamins in the prevention of cancer and cardiovascular disease: the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) randomized clinical trial. Am J Clin Nutr. 2022;115(6):1501-1510.
sources.finding: In 21,442 adults over 60, a daily multivitamin for 3.6 years did not significantly change total invasive cancer, cardiovascular events or all-cause death.

sources.citation: Shah SA, Chu BW, Lacey CS, et al. Impact of acute energy drink consumption on blood pressure parameters: a meta-analysis. Ann Pharmacother.
sources.finding: Pooling 15 studies, acute energy drink intake raised systolic pressure about 4.4 and diastolic about 2.7 mmHg; heart rate did not change significantly.

sources.citation: Shah SA, Szeto AH, Farewell R, et al. Impact of high volume energy drink consumption on electrocardiographic and blood pressure parameters: a randomized trial. J Am Heart Assoc.
sources.finding: In 34 healthy young adults, 32 oz of either energy drink lengthened the QTc interval more than placebo and raised blood pressure over four hours.

sources.citation: Sharma AK, Basu I, Singh S. Efficacy and safety of Ashwagandha root extract in subclinical hypothyroid patients: a double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial. J Altern Complement Med. 2018;24(3):243-248.
sources.finding: In 50 adults with raised TSH, 600 mg ashwagandha root extract daily for 8 weeks significantly shifted TSH, T3 and T4 versus placebo.

sources.citation: Shattock MJ, Tipton MJ. 'Autonomic conflict': a different way to die during cold water immersion? J Physiol 590(14):3219-3230.
sources.finding: Sudden cold immersion can trigger opposing heart-speeding and heart-slowing reflexes at once, which may explain frequent rhythm disturbances in healthy volunteers and some deaths in vulnerable people.

sources.citation: Siddiqui Z, Zufall A, Nash M, Rao D, Hirani R, Russo M. Comparing tretinoin to other topical therapies in the treatment of skin photoaging: a systematic review. Am J Clin Dermatol. 2024;25(6):873-890.
sources.finding: Across 25 studies comparing other topicals with tretinoin, tretinoin remained the benchmark; comparators were usually gentler, but most studies were low quality or biased.

sources.citation: Sitohang IBS, Makes WI, Sandora N, Suryanegara J. Topical tretinoin for treating photoaging: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials. Int J Womens Dermatol. 2022;8(1):e003.
sources.finding: Seven RCTs lasting 3 to 24 months consistently found topical tretinoin improved wrinkles, mottled pigmentation and sallowness, with changes seen from about one month.

sources.citation: Skotsimara G, Antonopoulos AS, Oikonomou E, et al. Cardiovascular effects of electronic cigarettes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Prev Cardiol. 2019;26(11):1219-1228.
sources.finding: Pooling 14 studies (441 people), vaping acutely raised heart rate by about 2 bpm and blood pressure by about 2 mmHg; most evidence came from non-randomized studies.

sources.citation: Sletten TL, Weaver MD, Foster RG, et al. The importance of sleep regularity: a consensus statement of the National Sleep Foundation sleep timing and variability panel. Sleep Health. 2023;9(6):801-820.
sources.finding: Expert panel reviewing 63 papers: regular sleep and wake timing matters for health, safety and performance; weekend catch-up sleep may help when weekday sleep falls short.

sources.citation: Spadola CE, Guo N, Johnson DA, et al. Evening intake of alcohol, caffeine, and nicotine: night-to-night associations with sleep duration and continuity among African Americans in the Jackson Heart Sleep Study. Sleep. 2019;42(11):zsz136.
sources.finding: Across 5,164 nights from 785 adults wearing actigraphs, nicotine within four hours of bedtime went with lower sleep efficiency and about six more minutes awake that night.

sources.citation: Sramek P, Simeckova M, Jansky L, Savlikova J, Vybiral S. Human physiological responses to immersion into water of different temperatures. Eur J Appl Physiol 81(5):436-442.
sources.finding: During one-hour head-out immersion at 14 C, young men's metabolic rate rose about 350 percent, noradrenaline about 530 percent and dopamine about 250 percent, with blood pressure up modestly.
sources.population: a small group of young men

sources.citation: Storoschuk KL, Moran-MacDonald A, Gibala MJ, Gurd BJ. Much ado about zone 2: a narrative review assessing the efficacy of zone 2 training for improving mitochondrial capacity and cardiorespiratory fitness in the general population. Sports Med 55(7):1611-1624.
sources.finding: Evidence does not show zone 2 is the best intensity for mitochondrial gains; enthusiasm leans on elite endurance athletes, and harder efforts matter more when weekly training time is low.
sources.population: general population (draws on athlete and training studies)

sources.citation: Treisman R. A study found lead in popular protein powders. Here's why you shouldn't panic. NPR, republished by OPB, 16 Oct 2025 (reporting Consumer Reports testing).
sources.finding: Consumer Reports tested 23 protein products; over two-thirds exceeded its strict per-day lead benchmark in one serving, and plant-based powders averaged nine times the lead of dairy ones.

sources.citation: Ucar C, Ucar C, Ozgocer T, Yildiz S. Effects of late-night eating of easily- or slowly-digestible meals on sleep, hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis, and autonomic nervous system in healthy young males. Stress Health.
sources.finding: In 16 young men, a heavy protein-and-fat meal at 10pm disturbed self-rated sleep, while short HRV recordings showed no change after either late meal.

sources.citation: US Code of Federal Regulations, 27 CFR 16.21: mandatory health warning statement on alcoholic beverage containers (read via Cornell LII).
sources.finding: US alcohol containers carry a government warning, citing the Surgeon General, against drinking in pregnancy because of birth-defect risk.

sources.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force; Mangione CM, Barry MJ, Nicholson WK, et al. Vitamin, mineral, and multivitamin supplementation to prevent cardiovascular disease and cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2022;327(23):2326-2333.
sources.finding: Evidence is insufficient to weigh multivitamins for heart disease or cancer in community-dwelling adults; the task force recommends against beta-carotene and vitamin E for these aims.

sources.citation: Vyas CM, Manson JE, Sesso HD, et al. Effect of multivitamin-mineral supplementation versus placebo on cognitive function: results from the clinic subcohort of the COSMOS randomized clinical trial and meta-analysis of 3 cognitive studies within COSMOS. Am J Clin Nutr. 2024;119(3):692-701.
sources.finding: Pooling three COSMOS cognitive studies, a daily multivitamin modestly improved global cognition and episodic memory, roughly two years less cognitive aging.

sources.citation: Wang Z, Qiu B, Li R, et al. Effects of creatine supplementation and resistance training on muscle strength gains in adults <50 years of age: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Nutrients. 2024;16(21):3665.
sources.finding: Across 23 RCTs in adults under 50 doing resistance training, creatine added about 4.4 kg upper-body and 11.4 kg lower-body strength versus placebo; data in women were sparse.
sources.population: adults under 50 doing resistance training, mostly young men

sources.citation: Wendsche J, Lohmann-Haislah A. A meta-analysis on antecedents and outcomes of detachment from work. Front Psychol. 2017;7:2072.
sources.finding: Across 91 samples (38,124 employees), mentally switching off from work went with better sleep and less exhaustion, and doing work tasks in off-hours went with less switching off.

sources.citation: Windred DP, Burns AC, Lane JM, et al. Sleep regularity is a stronger predictor of mortality risk than sleep duration: a prospective cohort study. Sleep. 2024;47(1):zsad253.
sources.finding: 60,977 UK adults with wrist-sensor data, about 6 years: more regular sleepers had 20% to 48% lower death risk than the least regular; regularity beat duration as a predictor.

sources.citation: Wright KP Jr, McHill AW, Birks BR, Griffin BR, Rusterholz T, Chinoy ED. Entrainment of the human circadian clock to the natural light-dark cycle. Curr Biol. 2013;23(16):1554-8.
sources.finding: After a summer week of camping under natural light only, eight adults' internal clocks moved about two hours earlier and lined up with sunrise and sunset.
sources.population: 8 healthy adults on a summer camping trip

sources.citation: Zhdanova IV, Wurtman RJ, Regan MM, Taylor JA, Shi JP, Leclair OU. Melatonin treatment for age-related insomnia. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2001;86(10):4727-4730.
sources.finding: In over-50s with insomnia, 0.1 to 3 mg all improved sleep, 3 mg with lower body temperature and daytime carryover; normal sleepers saw no change.
sources.population: 30 adults: insomniacs over 50 and normal sleepers

sources.citation: Wang WL, Chen KH, Pan YC, Yang SN, Chan YY. The effect of yoga on sleep quality and insomnia in women with sleep problems: a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Psychiatry. 2020;20:195.
sources.finding: Across 19 RCTs, yoga improved self-rated sleep quality a little. Insomnia severity didn't change, and breast cancer and menopause subgroups showed no clear effect.

sources.citation: Romeo A, Edney S, Plotnikoff R, et al. Can smartphone apps increase physical activity? Systematic review and meta-analysis. J Med Internet Res. 2019;21(3):e12053.
sources.finding: Activity apps raised daily steps by about 477 versus control, not statistically significant. Programmes shorter than three months did better than longer ones.

sources.citation: Villinger K, Wahl DR, Boeing H, Schupp HT, Renner B. The effectiveness of app-based mobile interventions on nutrition behaviours and nutrition-related health outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Obes Rev. 2019;20(10):1465-1484.
sources.finding: App-based nutrition interventions gave small benefits for eating behaviours and weight-related outcomes. Commercial and research apps performed similarly.

sources.citation: Simpson CC, Mazzeo SE. Calorie counting and fitness tracking technology: associations with eating disorder symptomatology. Eat Behav. 2017;26:89-92.
sources.finding: Students using calorie trackers reported more eating concern and dietary restraint, adjusting for BMI. Design can't show cause.

sources.citation: Hahn SL, Kaciroti N, Eisenberg D, Weeks HM, Bauer KW, Sonneville KR. Introducing dietary self-monitoring to undergraduate women via a calorie counting app has no effect on mental health or health behaviors: results from a randomized controlled trial. J Acad Nutr Diet. 2021;121(12):2377-2388.
sources.finding: One month of MyFitnessPal logging didn't change eating disorder risk, mood, body satisfaction or diet in low-risk women new to tracking.
sources.population: 200 undergraduate women at low eating disorder risk

sources.citation: Ferreira RM, Silva R, Vigário P, et al. The effects of massage guns on performance and recovery: a systematic review. J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. 2023;8(3):138.
sources.finding: Massage guns gave short-term gains in flexibility and less stiffness. Strength, power, balance and agility showed no gain or a drop.

sources.citation: Maia F, Nakamura FY, Sarmento H, Marcelino R, Ribeiro J. Effects of lower-limb intermittent pneumatic compression on sports recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Biol Sport. 2024;41(4):263-275.
sources.finding: Compression boots gave small reductions in soreness at some time points. Effects on muscle function were trivial; damage markers were unclear.

sources.citation: Chen W, Li X, Chen C. Whole-body vibration training and bone mineral density in older adults: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2026;27:149.
sources.finding: Vibration training slightly raised bone density at some hip sites. Total hip and most spine measures didn't change.

sources.citation: Rubio-Arias JÁ, Martínez-Aranda LM, Andreu-Caravaca L, et al. Effects of whole-body vibration training on body composition, cardiometabolic risk, and strength in the population who are overweight and obese: a systematic review with meta-analysis. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 2021;102(12):2442-2453.
sources.finding: Vibration training cut fat mass by about 1 kg, judged not clinically meaningful. Blood pressure fell and leg strength rose.
sources.population: 23 studies, 884 adults with overweight or obesity, mostly women

sources.citation: Reis-Silva A, Coelho-Oliveira AC, Moura-Fernandes MC, et al. Evidence of whole-body vibration exercises on body composition changes in older individuals: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Front Physiol. 2023;14:1202613.
sources.finding: Vibration exercise did not improve body composition in older adults.

sources.citation: Verma KK, Koch R, Gidwani K, et al. Facial contouring through jaw exercises: a report of two cases examining efficacy and consumer expectations. Cureus. 2024;16(11):e74635.
sources.finding: Three months of a commercial jaw exerciser gave no visible jawline or double-chin change. Users disliked gagging and suction.

sources.citation: Alam MK, Shayeb MA, Natarajan PM, et al. Association of temporomandibular disorders and other jaw anomalies in chewing gum users: a systematic review. J Oral Facial Pain Headache. 2025;39:35-47.
sources.finding: Findings were mixed: some studies tied more chewing to more jaw muscle discomfort, others found no link and symptoms that eased after stopping.

sources.citation: US Federal Trade Commission. FTC charges sellers of cell phone radiation protection patches with making false claims. Press release, 20 February 2002.
sources.finding: FTC alleged sellers' 97 to 99% blocking claims were unsupported. Independent lab tests found the patches did not reduce exposure.

sources.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. Do cell phones pose a health hazard? Content current as of 13 May 2021.
sources.finding: FDA says the weight of scientific evidence has not linked phone radio frequency energy with health problems.

sources.citation: Greco V, Bergamo D, Cuoccio P, Konkoly KR, Muñoz Lombardo K, Lewis PA. Wearing an eye mask during overnight sleep improves episodic learning and alertness. Sleep. 2023;46(3):zsac305.
sources.finding: A week of sleeping in an eye mask gave small gains in word-pair learning and reaction time versus no or holed mask; sleep stages unchanged.
sources.population: Young adults 18-35, two counterbalanced within-subject experiments (n=89, n=33)

sources.citation: Karimi L, Rahimi-Bashar F, Mohammadi SM, et al. The efficacy of eye masks and earplugs interventions for sleep promotion in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Front Psychiatry. 2021;12:791342.
sources.finding: Across 35 studies, eye masks and/or earplugs improved self-rated sleep quality; earplug-only results were mixed and heterogeneity high.
sources.population: Adult ICU and ward patients; three studies in healthy volunteers in simulated ICU

sources.citation: Hu RF, Jiang XY, Zeng YM, Chen XY, Zhang YH. Effects of earplugs and eye masks on nocturnal sleep, melatonin and cortisol in a simulated intensive care unit environment. Crit Care. 2010;14(2):R66.
sources.finding: Under recorded ICU noise and light, earplugs plus eye masks gave more REM sleep, fewer arousals and better perceived sleep; total sleep time not significant.
sources.population: 14 healthy adult volunteers, sleep lab, randomised night order

sources.citation: Riedy SM, Smith MG, Rocha S, Basner M. Noise as a sleep aid: a systematic review. Sleep Med Rev. 2021;55:101385.
sources.finding: Across 38 studies, evidence that continuous white noise improves sleep was very low quality; results ranged from better to more disrupted sleep.
sources.population: Human studies of continuous broadband noise, mixed populations

sources.citation: Singh S, Keller PR, Busija L, et al. Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2023;8:CD013244.
sources.finding: Six sleep RCTs (148 people): three found better sleep, three no difference. Very low certainty; effects on sleep unknown.
sources.population: Adults in 17 RCTs; six measured sleep

sources.citation: Thompson A, Jones H, Gregson W, Atkinson G. Effects of dawn simulation on markers of sleep inertia and post-waking performance in humans. Eur J Appl Physiol. 2014;114(5):1049-1056.
sources.finding: Dawn light in the last 30 minutes of sleep raised alertness and sleep-quality ratings and sped simple cognitive tasks; cycling performance gain not significant.
sources.population: 8 adults who report difficulty waking, random-order crossover

sources.citation: Golden RN, Gaynes BN, Ekstrom RD, et al. The efficacy of light therapy in the treatment of mood disorders: a review and meta-analysis of the evidence. Am J Psychiatry. 2005;162(4):656-662.
sources.finding: Bright light and dawn simulation reduced seasonal depression symptoms (effect sizes 0.84 and 0.73); bright light also helped non-seasonal depression.
sources.population: People with seasonal or non-seasonal depression in controlled trials

sources.citation: Pjrek E, Friedrich ME, Cambioli L, et al. The efficacy of light therapy in the treatment of seasonal affective disorder: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Psychother Psychosom. 2020;89(1):17-24.
sources.finding: Across 19 RCTs, bright light beat dim light or sham (SMD -0.37; response RR 1.42). Moderate heterogeneity, moderate-to-high risk of bias.

sources.citation: Takeshima M, Utsumi T, Aoki Y, et al. Efficacy and safety of bright light therapy for manic and depressive symptoms in patients with bipolar disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Psychiatry Clin Neurosci. 2020;74(4):247-256.
sources.finding: In six RCTs, mood switches were similar with light and control (4.7% on light); many took mood stabilisers. Long-term safety unknown.

sources.citation: Ekholm B, Spulber S, Adler M. A randomized controlled study of weighted chain blankets for insomnia in psychiatric disorders. J Clin Sleep Med. 2020;16(9):1567-1577.
sources.finding: After four weeks, 59% on weighted blankets halved insomnia scores versus 5% on light blankets; actigraphy sleep time unchanged.
sources.population: 120 adult psychiatric outpatients with insomnia (depression, bipolar, anxiety, ADHD)

sources.citation: Zhao Y, Zhang Q, Liu Z, Zhao Z, Zhu Q. Safety and effectiveness of weighted blankets for symptom management in patients with mental disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Complement Ther Med. 2024;87:103104.
sources.finding: Eight RCTs: small anxiety benefit; pooled insomnia effect not significant (p=0.06) until one study was dropped. No serious adverse events.

sources.citation: Trumka RL Jr. Beware: weighted infant swaddles and blankets are unsafe for sleep; retailers should consider stopping sales. US Consumer Product Safety Commission, commissioner statement, 15 April 2024.
sources.finding: CPSC, CDC, NIH and AAP warn against weighted blankets and swaddles for infants; multiple infant deaths are linked to weighted products.

sources.citation: Camacho M, Malu OO, Kram YA, et al. Nasal dilators (Breathe Right strips and NoZovent) for snoring and OSA: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Pulm Med. 2016;2016:4841310.
sources.finding: Across 14 mostly small studies, nasal dilators did not significantly change snoring index or sleep apnea severity, despite easier nasal breathing.
sources.population: 294 adults with snoring or obstructive sleep apnea

sources.citation: Wake Forest University Health Sciences (PI Fleischer AB), with Precision Fabrics Group. Efficacy of silk-like bedding fabric pillow case in the treatment of acne vulgaris. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00767104; completed 2009, results posted 2017.
sources.finding: After 12 weeks, lesion counts fell 13% on a silk-like synthetic pillowcase versus 22% on cotton; no benefit shown.
sources.population: 40 people with mild to severe facial acne

sources.citation: Chevalier G, Sinatra ST, Oschman JL, Sokal K, Sokal P. Earthing: health implications of reconnecting the human body to the Earth's surface electrons. J Environ Public Health. 2012;2012:291541.
sources.finding: Reviews small pilot studies reporting better sleep and less pain; the sleep study had 12 people and no control. Three authors hold company shares.

sources.citation: Lin CH, Tseng ST, Chuang YC, Kuo CE, Chen NC. Grounding the body improves sleep quality in patients with mild Alzheimer's disease: a pilot study. Healthcare (Basel). 2022;10(3):581.
sources.finding: Grounding mat sessions improved sleep-quality scores versus sham at 12 weeks (p=0.006), though the main model was borderline; 15 people completed.
sources.population: 22 older adults with mild Alzheimer's disease (15 completed)

sources.citation: Cleveland Clinic. Are there any health benefits to Himalayan salt lamps? Health Essentials, 20 April 2021 (Neha Vyas, MD).
sources.finding: Little evidence for any benefit; lamps emit too few negative ions to affect air, mood or sleep; claims are anecdotal.

sources.citation: Hemilä H, Chalker E. Vitamin C for preventing and treating the common cold. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2013;(1):CD000980.
sources.finding: Daily vitamin C (200 mg or more) did not cut cold incidence in the community but shortened colds 8% in adults, 14% in children; halved colds under heavy physical stress.
sources.population: placebo-controlled trials; 11,306 participants for incidence, 9,745 cold episodes for duration

sources.citation: Nault D, Machingo TA, Shipper AG, et al. Zinc for prevention and treatment of the common cold. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2024;5:CD014914.
sources.finding: Zinc to prevent colds may make little or no difference (low certainty). Started once a cold begins, it may shorten it about 2 days (low certainty), with more side effects.

sources.citation: Linus Pauling Institute Micronutrient Information Center. Zinc. Oregon State University; updated February 2019, reviewed May 2019.
sources.finding: Adult RDA is 11 mg (men) and 8 mg (women). Upper limit 40 mg/day, set to avoid copper deficiency; 60 mg/day total for 10 weeks caused signs of it.

sources.citation: Houston BL, Hurrie D, Graham J, et al. Efficacy of iron supplementation on fatigue and physical capacity in non-anaemic iron-deficient adults: a systematic review of randomised controlled trials. BMJ Open. 2018;8(4):e019240.
sources.finding: In iron-deficient adults without anaemia, iron reduced self-reported fatigue (SMD -0.38) and raised ferritin and haemoglobin, but did not improve measured exercise capacity.

sources.citation: Stoffel NU, Cercamondi CI, Brittenham G, et al. Iron absorption from oral iron supplements given on consecutive versus alternate days and as single morning doses versus twice-daily split dosing in iron-depleted women. Lancet Haematol. 2017;4(11):e524-e533.
sources.finding: Single 60 mg morning doses on alternate days were absorbed better than daily doses; splitting doses raised hepcidin and lowered absorption.
sources.population: 60 iron-depleted women aged 18 to 40 (ferritin 25 or below)

sources.citation: Linus Pauling Institute Micronutrient Information Center. Iron. Oregon State University; updated April 2016, reviewed May 2016.
sources.finding: RDA: 18 mg women 19 to 50, 8 mg men; upper limit 45 mg. Without medical evaluation, iron is advised against for people not at risk or with haemochromatosis.

sources.citation: Markun S, Gravestock I, Jäger L, et al. Effects of vitamin B12 supplementation on cognitive function, depressive symptoms, and fatigue: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression. Nutrients. 2021;13(3):923.
sources.finding: Without overt deficiency, B12 alone or with other B vitamins did not improve cognitive function or depressive symptoms; only one trial measured fatigue, too few to analyse.
sources.population: 16 RCTs, 6,276 adults without overt B12 deficiency

sources.citation: Niklewicz A, Hannibal L, Warren M, Ahmadi KR. A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional vitamin B12 status among adult vegans. Nutr Bull. 2024;49(4):463-479.
sources.finding: Vegans had lower B12 and higher homocysteine than omnivores, signs of functional deficiency; vegans taking B12 supplements had better levels on every marker.
sources.population: 17 observational studies of adult vegans, vegetarians and omnivores

sources.citation: Del Bo' C, Riso P, Gardana C, et al. Effect of two different sublingual dosages of vitamin B12 on cobalamin nutritional status in vegans and vegetarians with a marginal deficiency: a randomized controlled trial. Clin Nutr. 2019;38(2):575-583.
sources.finding: Both 350 mcg a week (about 50 mcg a day) and 2,000 mcg a week of sublingual B12 restored normal levels over 12 weeks, with no difference between doses.
sources.population: 40 vegans and vegetarians with marginal B12 deficiency

sources.citation: Linus Pauling Institute Micronutrient Information Center. Vitamin B12. Oregon State University; updated October 2023, reviewed November 2023.
sources.finding: Adult RDA 2.4 mcg; no upper limit. Only 1 to 2% of a large oral dose is absorbed. Vegans need a supplement; metformin and acid reducers can lower B12.

sources.citation: Zeng L, Yu G, Hao W, Yang K, Chen H. The efficacy and safety of Curcuma longa extract and curcumin supplements on osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Biosci Rep. 2021;41(6):BSR20210817.
sources.finding: Turmeric extract and curcumin reduced osteoarthritis pain and stiffness versus placebo and matched NSAIDs, with fewer side effects; authors suggest more than 12 weeks.

sources.citation: Fang W, Nasir Y. The effect of curcumin supplementation on recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage and delayed-onset muscle soreness: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Phytother Res. 2021;35(4):1768-1781.
sources.finding: Curcumin modestly lowered creatine kinase and muscle soreness scores after hard exercise; the authors note earlier individual trials were inconsistent.
sources.population: RCTs in adults after muscle-damaging exercise

sources.citation: Anand P, Kunnumakkara AB, Newman RA, Aggarwal BB. Bioavailability of curcumin: problems and promises. Mol Pharm. 2007;4(6):807-818.
sources.finding: Curcumin is safe at high doses but poorly absorbed, quickly metabolised and cleared; piperine, liposomes, nanoparticles and phospholipid complexes are used to raise absorption.
sources.population: review of human and lab studies

sources.citation: Halegoua-DeMarzio D, Navarro V, Ahmad J, et al. Liver injury associated with turmeric: a growing problem. Ten cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (DILIN). Am J Med. 2023;136(2):200-206.
sources.finding: Ten US cases of turmeric liver injury since 2011, five hospitalised and one death; latency 1 to 4 months, often with black pepper, strongly linked to HLA-B*35:01.

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH). Turmeric. Updated April 2025.
sources.finding: Early evidence for knee osteoarthritis pain is positive but needs higher quality. Highly absorbable curcumin products have been linked to liver injury; supplements may be unsafe in pregnancy.

sources.citation: Linus Pauling Institute Micronutrient Information Center. Curcumin. Oregon State University; updated February 2016, reviewed March 2016.
sources.finding: Oral curcumin has low systemic bioavailability. It inhibits platelet aggregation and may raise bleeding risk with warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or heparin.
sources.population: expert review of human and lab studies

sources.citation: Jovanovski E, Yashpal S, Komishon A, et al. Effect of psyllium (Plantago ovata) fiber on LDL cholesterol and alternative lipid targets, non-HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Am J Clin Nutr. 2018;108(5):922-932.
sources.finding: A median 10.2 g/day of psyllium lowered LDL cholesterol by 0.33 mmol/L, plus non-HDL cholesterol and apoB, in people with or without high cholesterol.

sources.citation: van der Schoot A, Drysdale C, Whelan K, Dimidi E. The effect of fiber supplementation on chronic constipation in adults: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Am J Clin Nutr. 2022;116(4):953-969.
sources.finding: Fibre supplements helped 66% versus 41% on control; psyllium worked best, above 10 g/day for at least 4 weeks. More wind was the main side effect.

sources.citation: Kim MG, Yang I, Lee HS, Lee JY, Kim K. Lipid-modifying effects of krill oil vs fish oil: a network meta-analysis. Nutr Rev. 2020;78(9):699-708.
sources.finding: Krill oil and fish oil did not differ in effects on triglycerides, LDL, HDL or total cholesterol; triglyceride lowering depended on the omega-3 dose.
sources.population: 64 RCTs of krill oil or fish oil

sources.citation: Laslett LL, Scheepers LEJM, Antony B, et al. Krill oil for knee osteoarthritis: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2024;331(23):1997-2006.
sources.finding: 2 g/day of krill oil for 24 weeks did not reduce knee pain more than placebo.
sources.population: 262 adults with painful knee osteoarthritis, mean age 62

sources.citation: NOW Foods. Neptune Krill Oil 1000 mg, 60 softgels. Supplement Facts as listed by Vitasave (retailer).
sources.finding: One 1,000 mg softgel lists 120 mg EPA and 70 mg DHA, 230 mg total omega-3.

sources.citation: Qu H, Guo M, Chai H, et al. Effects of coenzyme Q10 on statin-induced myopathy: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. J Am Heart Assoc. 2018;7(19):e009835.
sources.finding: CoQ10 eased statin-associated muscle pain, weakness, cramps and tiredness versus placebo, without changing creatine kinase.
sources.population: 12 RCTs, 575 statin users with muscle symptoms

sources.citation: Kennedy C, Köller Y, Surkova E. Effect of coenzyme Q10 on statin-associated myalgia and adherence to statin therapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Atherosclerosis. 2020;299:1-8.
sources.finding: CoQ10 did not improve statin-associated muscle pain or help people stay on statins; only two of eight trials found a benefit.

sources.citation: Kovacic S, Habicht SD, Eckert GP. Effects of coenzyme Q10 supplementation on myopathy in statin-treated patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Nutr Sci. 2025;14:e72.
sources.finding: 100 to 600 mg/day CoQ10 slightly reduced statin muscle pain overall; four trials found a reduction, three did not.

sources.citation: Tsai IC, Hsu CW, Chang CH, Tseng PT, Chang KV. Effectiveness of coenzyme Q10 supplementation for reducing fatigue: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Front Pharmacol. 2022;13:883251.
sources.finding: CoQ10 reduced fatigue scores versus placebo (g -0.40), in healthy and ill participants alike; higher doses and longer use went with larger effects.

sources.citation: Deng H, Song T, Yin M, et al. Coenzyme Q10 supplementation increases blood concentrations but shows limited and inconsistent effects on exercise performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Br J Nutr. 2025.
sources.finding: CoQ10 reliably raised blood levels, but effects on exercise performance were small, unstable and of low to very low certainty; fatigue findings were suggestive.

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH). Coenzyme Q10. Updated January 2019.
sources.finding: Overall evidence does not support CoQ10 for statin muscle pain; heart failure research is inconclusive. No serious side effects reported; may interact with warfarin.

sources.citation: Bamford JT, Ray S, Musekiwa A, et al. Oral evening primrose oil and borage oil for eczema. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2013;(4):CD004416.
sources.finding: Evening primrose and borage oil did no better than placebo for eczema symptoms; confidence intervals were narrow enough to make further trials hard to justify.
sources.population: 27 RCTs, 1,596 children and adults with eczema

sources.citation: Budeiri D, Li Wan Po A, Dornan JC. Is evening primrose oil of value in the treatment of premenstrual syndrome? Control Clin Trials. 1996;17(1):60-68.
sources.finding: Only seven placebo-controlled PMS trials; the two best-controlled showed no benefit. Small trials cannot exclude modest effects.
sources.population: 7 placebo-controlled trials in women with PMS

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH). Evening primrose oil. Updated November 2024.
sources.finding: Oral evening primrose oil has not been shown to help eczema, is probably no better than placebo for breast pain, and evidence for PMS and menopause is insufficient.

sources.citation: Khalesi S, Bellissimo N, Vandelanotte C, et al. A review of probiotic supplementation in healthy adults: helpful or hype? Eur J Clin Nutr. 2019;73(1):24-37.
sources.finding: In healthy adults, probiotics briefly raised the supplemented bacteria and had some support for stool consistency and immune markers, but no lasting microbiome change or lipid benefit.

sources.citation: Rauch CE, Mika AS, McCubbin AJ, Huschtscha Z, Costa RJS. Effect of prebiotics, probiotics, and synbiotics on gastrointestinal outcomes in healthy adults and active adults at rest and in response to exercise: a systematic literature review. Front Nutr. 2022;9:1003620.
sources.finding: Probiotics raised the supplemented strain but did not improve gut symptoms, permeability or other gut markers in healthy adults, at rest or during exercise.
sources.population: 37 papers, 1,204 healthy sedentary and active adults

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NIH). Probiotics: what you need to know. Updated August 2019.
sources.finding: Effects differ by strain; for most conditions it is unclear which probiotics help. Risks are higher with serious illness or weakened immunity; some products contain unlisted microbes.

sources.citation: Linus Pauling Institute Micronutrient Information Center. Vitamin C. Oregon State University.
sources.finding: Up to 200 mg at a time is fully absorbed; blood levels plateau at 200 to 400 mg/day. Upper limit 2 g/day; stone-prone people may avoid 1 g/day or more.

sources.citation: Vickers AJ, Vertosick EA, Lewith G, et al. Acupuncture for chronic pain: update of an individual patient data meta-analysis. J Pain. 2018;19(5):455-474.
sources.finding: Acupuncture beat sham (about 0.2 SD) and no acupuncture (about 0.5 SD) for four chronic pain conditions; effects mostly persisted at one year.
sources.population: 20,827 adults with chronic musculoskeletal, osteoarthritis, headache or shoulder pain in 39 RCTs

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. Acupuncture: Effectiveness and Safety. nccih.nih.gov, last updated October 2022.
sources.finding: Acupuncture helps chronic back, neck, knee osteoarthritis pain and migraine frequency, modestly over sham. Serious harms are rare and tied to non-sterile needles or poor technique.

sources.citation: Rubinstein SM, de Zoete A, van Middelkoop M, Assendelft WJJ, de Boer MR, van Tulder MW. Benefits and harms of spinal manipulative therapy for the treatment of chronic low back pain: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. BMJ. 2019;364:l689.
sources.finding: Spinal manipulation gave similar short-term pain relief to other recommended therapies and slightly better function; adverse events were mostly mild and transient.
sources.population: 9,211 adults with chronic low back pain in 47 RCTs

sources.citation: Eklund A, Jensen I, Lohela-Karlsson M, et al. The Nordic Maintenance Care program: effectiveness of chiropractic maintenance care versus symptom-guided treatment for recurrent and persistent low back pain. PLoS One. 2018;13(9):e0203029.
sources.finding: Scheduled maintenance visits gave 12.8 fewer days with bothersome back pain over a year than symptom-guided care, with about 1.7 more visits.
sources.population: 328 adults 18-65 with recurrent or persistent low back pain who responded well to initial chiropractic care

sources.citation: Shi Q, Wang Y, Hao Q, et al. Pharmacotherapy for adults with overweight and obesity: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. Lancet. 2024;403(10434):e21-e31 (retracted and republished from Lancet 2022;399:259-269).
sources.finding: All weight-lowering drugs beat lifestyle alone; GLP-1 drugs gave about 5.8% extra weight loss and semaglutide about 11.4%, with more side-effect dropouts.
sources.population: 48,209 adults with overweight or obesity in 132 RCTs

sources.citation: Wilding JPH, Batterham RL, Calanna S, et al. Once-weekly semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity. N Engl J Med. 2021;384(11):989-1002.
sources.finding: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly plus lifestyle cut body weight 14.9% vs 2.4% on placebo over 68 weeks; nausea and diarrhoea were common.
sources.population: 1,961 adults without diabetes, BMI 30+ or 27+ with a weight-related condition

sources.citation: Bhasin S, Brito JP, Cunningham GR, et al. Testosterone therapy in men with hypogonadism: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2018;103(5):1715-1744.
sources.finding: Diagnose low testosterone only with symptoms and repeated low fasting morning levels; avoid therapy when planning fertility, with prostate cancer, high hematocrit, untreated severe sleep apnea or recent heart events.

sources.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. FDA's concerns with unapproved GLP-1 drugs used for weight loss. fda.gov, content current as of 2026-10-01.
sources.finding: Compounded GLP-1s are not FDA-reviewed; dosing errors caused hospitalisations, salt forms lack a lawful basis, counterfeits exist; get a prescription and use a licensed pharmacy.
sources.population: US consumers using compounded or unapproved semaglutide or tirzepatide

sources.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. Certain bulk drug substances for use in compounding that may present significant safety risks. fda.gov, content current as of 2026-04-22.
sources.finding: BPC-157, TB-500, CJC-1295, ipamorelin and other peptides are listed with little or no human safety data and possible immune reactions from impurities.
sources.population: compounded peptide products in the US

sources.citation: Trauer JM, Qian MY, Doyle JS, Rajaratnam SM, Cunnington D. Cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Ann Intern Med. 2015;163(3):191-204.
sources.finding: CBT-I cut time to fall asleep by about 19 minutes and night waking by 26 minutes, raised sleep efficiency about 10%, with sustained effects.
sources.population: 1,162 adults with chronic insomnia in 20 RCTs

sources.citation: Mitchell LJ, Ball LE, Ross LJ, Barnes KA, Williams LT. Effectiveness of dietetic consultations in primary health care: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials. J Acad Nutr Diet. 2017;117(12):1941-1962.
sources.finding: Dietitian consultations improved diet quality, blood sugar and weight measures versus comparators; evidence for lipids and blood pressure was limited.
sources.population: 5,500 adults in primary care across 26 RCTs

sources.citation: Williams LT, Barnes K, Ball L, Ross LJ, Sladdin I, Mitchell LJ. How effective are dietitians in weight management? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Healthcare (Basel). 2019;7(1):20.
sources.finding: Individual dietitian care gave about 1 kg more weight loss and 0.4 lower BMI than usual care; trial risk of bias was unclear to high.
sources.population: adults in 14 RCTs (1,598 in the weight meta-analysis)

sources.citation: Krogsbøll LT, Jørgensen KJ, Gøtzsche PC. General health checks in adults for reducing morbidity and mortality from disease. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2019;1:CD009009.
sources.finding: General health checks had little or no effect on total, cancer or cardiovascular deaths (high certainty) and are unlikely to be beneficial.
sources.population: about 250,000 adults without symptoms in 17 randomised trials

sources.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for vitamin D deficiency in adults: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325(14):1436-1442.
sources.finding: Evidence is insufficient to weigh benefits and harms of vitamin D screening in adults without symptoms; no single level defines deficiency.

sources.citation: Makkena HB, Nimmagadda Y, Boinapelly N, et al. Behavioral and psychosocial effects of participant-visible continuous glucose monitoring in adults without diabetes: a systematic review. Medicina (Kaunas). 2026;62(9):1814.
sources.finding: Twelve studies; CGM may support some diet changes alongside education, but certainty is low and lasting or standalone benefit is not established.

sources.citation: Shah VN, DuBose SN, Li Z, et al. Continuous glucose monitoring profiles in healthy nondiabetic participants: a multicenter prospective study. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2019;104(10):4356-4364.
sources.finding: Healthy people spent a median 96% of the day between 70 and 140 mg/dL; mean glucose about 98 to 99 mg/dL under 60.
sources.population: 153 healthy non-diabetic people aged 7 to 80 wearing a blinded CGM

sources.citation: Celis-Morales C, Livingstone KM, Marsaux CF, et al. Effect of personalized nutrition on health-related behaviour change: evidence from the Food4Me European randomized controlled trial. Int J Epidemiol. 2017;46(2):578-588.
sources.finding: Personalised diet advice beat generic advice, but adding blood markers or genotype gave no extra improvement in diet.

sources.citation: Gardner CD, Trepanowski JF, Del Gobbo LC, et al. Effect of low-fat vs low-carbohydrate diet on 12-month weight loss in overweight adults and the association with genotype pattern or insulin secretion: the DIETFITS randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2018;319(7):667-679.
sources.finding: Low-fat and low-carb diets gave similar 12-month weight loss; a three-gene pattern did not predict who lost more on either diet.
sources.population: 609 adults 18 to 50 without diabetes, BMI 28 to 40

sources.citation: Catanese L (reviewed by Shmerling RH). Hyperbaric oxygen therapy: evidence-based uses and unproven claims. Harvard Health Publishing, 2024-12-09.
sources.finding: HBOT is FDA-cleared for conditions like decompression sickness, carbon monoxide poisoning and hard-to-heal wounds; many marketed claims are unapproved; ear, sinus and fire risks exist.
sources.population: general (summary of FDA-cleared uses and risks)

sources.citation: Hadanny A, Daniel-Kotovsky M, Suzin G, et al. Cognitive enhancement of healthy older adults using hyperbaric oxygen: a randomized controlled trial. Aging (Albany NY). 2020;12(13):13740-13761.
sources.finding: Three months of HBOT improved attention and processing speed scores versus control; authors work for or hold shares in a company selling HBOT.

sources.citation: Hachmo Y, Hadanny A, Abu Hamed R, et al. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy increases telomere length and decreases immunosenescence in isolated blood cells: a prospective trial. Aging (Albany NY). 2020;12(22):22445-22456.
sources.finding: Uncontrolled study: blood-cell telomere length rose over 20% after 60 sessions; authors work for or hold shares in a company selling HBOT.
sources.population: 35 healthy adults 64 and older, no control group

sources.citation: Ezzo J, Manheimer E, McNeely ML, et al. Manual lymphatic drainage for lymphedema following breast cancer treatment. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2015;(5):CD003475.
sources.finding: Added to compression bandaging, lymphatic drainage gave about 7% more arm-volume reduction in two small trials; other comparisons were not significant or too varied.
sources.population: women with breast cancer-related lymphedema in 6 trials

sources.citation: Acosta RD, Cash BD. Clinical effects of colonic cleansing for general health promotion: a systematic review. Am J Gastroenterol. 2009;104(11):2830-2836.
sources.finding: No methodologically rigorous controlled trials support colon cleansing for general health; multiple case reports and series describe adverse effects.

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. Detoxes and cleanses: what you need to know. nccih.nih.gov, last updated March 2025.
sources.finding: Cleanse studies are few and low quality; weight lost is usually regained. Colonics can cause serious side effects, more likely with kidney, heart or bowel disease.

sources.citation: Wolfe RR. Branched-chain amino acids and muscle protein synthesis in humans: myth or reality? J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:30.
sources.finding: No human studies show oral BCAAs alone raise muscle protein synthesis; two infusion studies saw it fall. All essential amino acids are needed.

sources.citation: Salem A, Ben Maaoui K, Jahrami H, et al. Attenuating muscle damage biomarkers and muscle soreness after an exercise-induced muscle damage with branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) supplementation: a systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression. Sports Med Open. 2024;10:42.
sources.finding: Across 18 RCTs, BCAAs lowered soreness 24 to 96 hours after damaging exercise and creatine kinase at some points; high heterogeneity and some publication bias.

sources.citation: Gleeson M. Dosing and efficacy of glutamine supplementation in human exercise and sport training. J Nutr. 2008;138(10):2045S-2049S.
sources.finding: Claimed immune, glycogen and anti-breakdown benefits have little support in well-controlled studies of healthy, well-nourished people. 20 to 30 g doses appeared harmless.

sources.citation: Ramezani Ahmadi A, Rayyani E, Bahreini M, Mansoori A. The effect of glutamine supplementation on athletic performance, body composition, and immune function: a systematic review and a meta-analysis of clinical trials. Clin Nutr. 2019;38(3):1076-1091.
sources.finding: Across 25 trials, glutamine did not change immune markers, aerobic performance or body composition; a small extra weight drop was seen.

sources.citation: Candow DG, Chilibeck PD, Burke DG, Davison KS, Smith-Palmer T. Effect of glutamine supplementation combined with resistance training in young adults. Eur J Appl Physiol. 2001;86(2):142-149.
sources.finding: Six weeks of high-dose glutamine with lifting gave no extra strength, lean mass or change in muscle breakdown versus placebo.

sources.citation: Koehler K, Parr MK, Geyer H, Mester J, Schanzer W. Serum testosterone and urinary excretion of steroid hormone metabolites after administration of a high-dose zinc supplement. Eur J Clin Nutr. 2009;63(1):65-70.
sources.finding: ZMA raised blood zinc but did not change total or free testosterone in men already eating enough zinc.

sources.citation: Wilborn CD, Kerksick CM, Campbell BI, et al. Effects of zinc magnesium aspartate (ZMA) supplementation on training adaptations and markers of anabolism and catabolism. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2004;1(2):12-20.
sources.finding: Eight weeks of nightly ZMA during training changed no hormones, body composition, strength or anaerobic capacity versus placebo.

sources.citation: Edwards BJ, Adam RL, Drummond D, et al. Effects of an acute dose of zinc monomethionine aspartate and magnesium aspartate (ZMA) on subsequent sleep and next-day morning performance. Nutrients. 2024;16(15):2466.
sources.finding: Two nights of ZMA had no effect on measured sleep, sprints or attention compared with placebo, in men with adequate diets.

sources.citation: Chun N, Aman S, Xu D, et al. Anemia due to unexpected zinc-induced copper deficiency. Hematol Rep. 2025;17(4):35.
sources.finding: Years of high-dose zinc supplements led to copper deficiency with anemia and low white cells, which can be mistaken for other blood disorders.

sources.citation: Qureshi A, Naughton DP, Petroczi A. A systematic review on the herbal extract Tribulus terrestris and the roots of its putative aphrodisiac and performance enhancing effect. J Diet Suppl. 2014;11(1):64-79.
sources.finding: Across 11 studies, tribulus did not raise testosterone in humans except as part of combined supplements; marketing claims are unsubstantiated.

sources.citation: Willoughby DS, Leutholtz B. D-aspartic acid supplementation combined with 28 days of heavy resistance training has no effect on body composition, muscle strength, and serum hormones associated with the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis in resistance-trained men. Nutr Res. 2013;33(10):803-810.
sources.finding: 3 g a day of D-aspartic acid for 28 days changed neither testosterone nor strength or body composition versus placebo.

sources.citation: Melville GW, Siegler JC, Marshall PWM. The effects of d-aspartic acid supplementation in resistance-trained men over a three month training period: a randomised controlled trial. PLoS One. 2017;12(8):e0182630.
sources.finding: 6 g a day for 12 weeks did not change testosterone or training gains; estradiol fell 16%.

sources.citation: Mansoori A, Hosseini S, Hosseini S, et al. Effect of fenugreek extract supplement on testosterone levels in male: a meta-analysis of clinical trials. Phytother Res. 2020;34(7):1550-1555.
sources.finding: Pooling four randomized trials, fenugreek extract significantly raised total testosterone in men; effect size not given in the abstract.

sources.citation: Clemesha CG, Thaker H, Samplaski MK. 'Testosterone boosting' supplements composition and claims are not supported by the academic literature. World J Mens Health. 2020;38(1):115-122.
sources.finding: Of 109 ingredients in 50 products, 24.8% had data showing a testosterone rise; 13 products exceeded upper limits for zinc, B3 or magnesium.

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. Fenugreek. Updated February 2025.
sources.finding: Fenugreek above food amounts is not safe in pregnancy; large doses may drop blood sugar harmfully; evidence for most uses is limited.

sources.citation: Jeukendrup AE, Randell R. Fat burners: nutrition supplements that increase fat metabolism. Obes Rev. 2011;12(10):841-851.
sources.finding: Of popular fat-burner ingredients, only caffeine and green tea have data for raising fat metabolism; evidence for the rest is lacking.

sources.citation: Tabrizi R, Saneei P, Lankarani KB, et al. The effects of caffeine intake on weight loss: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr. 2019;59(16):2688-2696.
sources.finding: Across 13 RCTs, more caffeine went with slightly more weight, BMI and fat loss, but results varied very widely between trials.

sources.citation: Jurgens TM, Whelan AM, Killian L, et al. Green tea for weight loss and weight maintenance in overweight or obese adults. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2012;(12):CD008650.
sources.finding: Outside Japan, green tea preparations changed weight by -0.04 kg over 12 weeks, an effect too small to matter.

sources.citation: Batsis JA, Apolzan JW, Bagley PJ, et al. A systematic review of dietary supplements and alternative therapies for weight loss. Obesity (Silver Spring). 2021;29(7):1102-1113.
sources.finding: Of 315 RCTs, only 52 were low risk and sufficient; 16 of those showed weight differences of 0.3 to 4.9 kg.

sources.citation: Geller AI, Shehab N, Weidle NJ, et al. Emergency department visits for adverse events related to dietary supplements. N Engl J Med. 2015;373(16):1531-1540.
sources.finding: Weight-loss or energy products caused 71.8% of supplement-related ER visits for palpitations, chest pain or racing heart; 58% involved people aged 20 to 34.

sources.citation: Pomeroy DE, Tooley KL, Probert B, Wilson A, Kemps E. A systematic review of the effect of dietary supplements on cognitive performance in healthy young adults and military personnel. Nutrients. 2020;12(2):545.
sources.finding: Of 37 studies, 73% were low quality; only tyrosine or caffeine had support, mainly under sleep loss. Other supplements showed inconsistent findings.

sources.citation: Camfield DA, Stough C, Farrimond J, Scholey AB. Acute effects of tea constituents L-theanine, caffeine, and epigallocatechin gallate on cognitive function and mood: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Nutr Rev. 2014;72(8):507-522.
sources.finding: Caffeine with L-theanine gave moderate gains in alertness and attention switching in the first two hours, tracking caffeine dose more than theanine.

sources.citation: Marcus L, Soileau J, Judge LW, Bellar D. Evaluation of the effects of two doses of alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine on physical and psychomotor performance. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:39.
sources.finding: A week of alpha-GPC did not change attention or strength tests; 250 mg improved jump power and 500 mg lowered TSH.

sources.citation: Lee G, Choi S, Chang J, et al. Association of L-alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine with subsequent stroke risk after 10 years. JAMA Netw Open. 2021;4(11):e2136008.
sources.finding: Adults prescribed alpha-GPC had about 43% higher 10-year stroke risk than matched non-users, rising with longer use.
sources.population: 12 million South Korean adults aged 50 and over

sources.citation: Cohen PA, Avula B, Wang YH, Zakharevich I, Khan I. Five unapproved drugs found in cognitive enhancement supplements. Neurol Clin Pract. 2021;11(3):e303-e307.
sources.finding: Ten cognitive supplements held five unapproved drugs, some undeclared, at up to four times drug doses; 75% of labeled amounts were wrong.

sources.citation: Stellingwerff T, Cox GR. Systematic review: carbohydrate supplementation on exercise performance or capacity of varying durations. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab. 2014;39(9):998-1011.
sources.finding: In 82% of 61 trials, carbohydrate during exercise improved performance versus water, with bigger gains in longer sessions.

sources.citation: Docherty S, Doughty FL, Smith EF. The acute and chronic effects of lion's mane mushroom supplementation on cognitive function, stress and mood in young adults: a double-blind, parallel groups, pilot study. Nutrients. 2023;15(22):4842.
sources.finding: One 1.8 g dose sped a Stroop task at 60 minutes; 28 days showed only a non-significant trend to less stress, plus some null results.

sources.citation: Menon A, et al. Benefits, side effects, and uses of Hericium erinaceus as a supplement: a systematic review. Front Nutr. 2025;12:1641246.
sources.finding: Five RCTs and three pilot trials, mostly in people with or without dementia; small memory-score gains. Most other evidence was lab or animal. Side effects: stomach upset, headache, allergy.
sources.population: Human trials plus lab and animal studies, 2000 to 2024

sources.citation: RYZE Superfoods. RYZE Mushroom Coffee, product page (brand).
sources.finding: One bag holds 30 servings, listed at $45, shown at $27 on sale. The page states no mushroom amounts.

sources.citation: Joseph M. RYZE Mushroom Coffee: does it have benefits? Nutrition Advance. Updated March 2024.
sources.finding: Citing the company, a serving holds 2 g of a six-mushroom blend and 48 mg caffeine, about half a typical coffee.

sources.citation: Aakre I, et al. Commercially available kelp and seaweed products: valuable iodine source or risk of excess intake? Food Nutr Res. 2021;65:7584.
sources.finding: Iodine per portion or dose varied hugely; 54 of 96 seaweed foods and supplements would exceed the iodine upper limit in one serving. Labels were often inaccurate.
sources.population: 96 seaweed foods and supplements sold in Norway

sources.citation: Rejuso A, et al. Microbial and heavy metal analyses of commercially available sea moss and sea moss products. J Food Prot. 2026;100915.
sources.finding: Dried sea moss contained arsenic, cobalt and mercury; gels had trace mercury. Bacteria including Salmonella and Cronobacter were isolated from some products. Quality varied widely.
sources.population: 66 sea moss products bought from major US online retailers

sources.citation: Taylor PN, et al. What endocrinologists should know about iodine: population deficiency, individual excess and misinformation in the United Kingdom. Clin Endocrinol. 2026.
sources.finding: Social-media wellness trends push kelp supplements delivering iodine far above recommended intake; endocrinologists are seeing more iodine-induced thyroid dysfunction alongside population deficiency.
sources.population: UK population and clinic patients (narrative review)

sources.citation: Pandit S, et al. Clinical evaluation of purified Shilajit on testosterone levels in healthy volunteers. Andrologia. 2016;48(5):570-5.
sources.finding: Purified shilajit (PrimaVie) 250 mg twice daily for 90 days raised total and free testosterone and DHEAS versus placebo. Funded by Natreon, the extract's maker.

sources.citation: Yadav D, et al. Safety and efficacy of TruBlk Shilajit resin supplementation on physical performance and blood biomarkers in healthy adults: a 28-day open-label pilot study. Cureus. 2026.
sources.finding: Open-label, no placebo: 500 mg/day resin for 28 days with within-group strength and fatigue gains. Most authors work for the brand, Amaara Botanicals.

sources.citation: Kamgar E, et al. Quantifying of thallium in Shilajit and its supplements to unveil the potential risk of consumption of this popular traditional medicine. BMC Chem. 2025;19.
sources.finding: Thallium, a toxic metal, was found in raw shilajit and shilajit supplements; some supplements held more than raw resin. Authors call for routine testing.
sources.population: Raw shilajit and commercial shilajit supplements from several regions

sources.citation: Morgado A, et al. Do 'testosterone boosters' really increase serum total testosterone? A systematic review. Int J Impot Res. 2024.
sources.finding: Most of 27 marketed testosterone boosters failed to raise testosterone. Tongkat ali rated possibly effective in healthy and low-testosterone men; purified shilajit possibly effective in low-testosterone men.
sources.population: 52 studies in athletes, healthy men, infertile men and men with low testosterone

sources.citation: Docherty S, Doughty FL, Smith EF. The acute and chronic effects of lion's mane mushroom supplementation on cognitive function, stress and mood in young adults: a double-blind, parallel groups, pilot study. Nutrients. 2023;15(22):4842.
sources.finding: 1.8 g/day: one dose sped a single attention task; after 28 days no cognitive benefit and only a non-significant trend toward lower stress. Product donated by Sempera Organics.

sources.citation: Surendran G, et al. Acute effects of a standardised extract of Hericium erinaceus (Lion's Mane mushroom) on cognition and mood in healthy younger adults: a double-blind randomised placebo-controlled study. Front Nutr. 2025;12:1405796.
sources.finding: One 3 g extract dose had no overall effect on cognition or mood; only a pegboard task improved. Two authors work for a lion's mane drinks brand.

sources.citation: Shin BC, Lee MS, Yang EJ, Lim HS, Ernst E. Maca (L. meyenii) for improving sexual function: a systematic review. BMC Complement Altern Med. 2010;10:44.
sources.finding: Four small RCTs (131 people, 1.5 to 3.5 g/day): three showed some benefit for sexual desire or function, one none. Too few and too weak for firm conclusions.
sources.population: Healthy men, postmenopausal women, cyclists and men with mild erectile dysfunction

sources.citation: Ho CY, Hsu CH, Chien TJ. Herbal dietary supplements for erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials. J Tradit Complement Med. 2026.
sources.finding: Across 14 RCTs, saffron and ginseng showed benefits; evidence for maca and Tribulus remained insufficient, needing larger, longer trials.
sources.population: 1,227 men with erectile dysfunction aged 35 to 65

sources.citation: Jones AW, March DS, Curtis F, Bridle C. Bovine colostrum supplementation and upper respiratory symptoms during exercise training: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil. 2016;8:21.
sources.finding: Five small trials, 10 to 20 g/day for 8 to 12 weeks, cut cold-symptom days by about 44%. Four of five had moderate or high bias risk.

sources.citation: Aitkenhead R, et al. The influence of dietary supplements on exercise-induced gut damage and gastrointestinal symptoms: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Nutrients. 2025;17(3):443.
sources.finding: Across 26 studies of supplements for exercise gut stress, no pooled benefit on gut symptoms or performance; the few significant changes were too small to matter clinically.
sources.population: Healthy adults doing endurance exercise, often in heat

sources.citation: Goluch Z, et al. The effects of Colostrum bovinum supplementation on human body fat content and/or blood lipid profile: a systematic review of clinical trials. Nutrients. 2026;18(10):1579.
sources.finding: Thirteen trials gave inconsistent, heterogeneous results on body fat and blood lipids; a few small benefits appeared at 10 to 60 g/day.
sources.population: Adults including older adults and people with type 2 diabetes

sources.citation: Yang W, et al. Safety and metabolism-related outcomes of oral nicotinamide mononucleotide supplementation in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Nutrients. 2026;18(14):2251.
sources.finding: Fifteen RCTs (250 to 2,000 mg/day, up to 24 weeks): NMN was well tolerated but did not change weight, fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids or systolic pressure.
sources.population: Adults, many older or with early metabolic risk

sources.citation: Gallagher C, Emmanuel OO. NAD+ supplementation for anti-aging and wellness: a PRISMA-guided systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence. Ageing Res Rev. 2026;103057.
sources.finding: In 33 human studies, NR and NMN reliably raised NAD markers and were well tolerated, but functional and healthspan outcomes were mostly null or inconsistent.
sources.population: Human and rodent intervention studies, 2010 to 2025

sources.citation: Gao Y, et al. Domain-specific effects of NAD+ precursors on fatigue and functional performance: a systematic review and network meta-analysis. Front Nutr. 2026.
sources.finding: No NAD precursor improved felt fatigue or sleep. NMN was linked to better endurance at medium and high doses; strength did not change.

sources.citation: Zhao JV, et al. Overall and sex-specific effect of berberine on glycemic and insulin-related traits: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. J Nutr. 2023;153(10).
sources.finding: Twenty placebo-controlled RCTs: berberine lowered fasting glucose by about 0.5 mmol/L and HbA1c, with larger effects in people with diabetes.
sources.population: 1,761 adults, many with diabetes or metabolic disease

sources.citation: Liu D, et al. Efficacy and safety of berberine on the components of metabolic syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials. Front Pharmacol. 2025;16:1572197.
sources.finding: Twelve RCTs (300 to 1,500 mg/day, 12 to 20 weeks) lowered triglycerides, fasting glucose and waist; stomach side effects not significantly above placebo.
sources.population: 889 adults with metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, dyslipidemia or PCOS

sources.citation: Elahi Vahed I, et al. The effect of berberine on obesity indices: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Int J Obes. 2026.
sources.finding: Across 23 RCTs berberine reduced body weight by about 0.9 kg and waist slightly; many trials lacked proper blinding or randomisation.
sources.population: Adults in randomized trials, mostly with metabolic conditions

sources.citation: Dumitru CN, et al. Berberine-drug interactions: mechanisms, clinical relevance and risk stratification: a narrative review. Pharmaceuticals. 2026;19(8):1313.
sources.finding: Berberine inhibits CYP3A4, CYP2D6 and CYP2C9, alters drug transporters and adds to low blood sugar and blood pressure; it raised cyclosporine levels in transplant patients.
sources.population: Human, animal and lab interaction studies

sources.citation: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. Goldenseal. Last updated February 2025.
sources.finding: Goldenseal (a berberine source) cut metformin levels about 25% in healthy adults. Not for pregnancy, breastfeeding or infants; berberine can harm newborns.

sources.citation: Jeyaraman MM, et al. Resveratrol for adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2020;CD011919.
sources.finding: Three small RCTs (50 people, 4 to 5 weeks) showed no effect on HbA1c, fasting glucose or insulin resistance; evidence insufficient either way.

sources.citation: Sun JN, et al. Effects of resveratrol supplementation on multiple health outcomes: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials. Nutr J. 2026.
sources.finding: Of 129 associations, four had high-certainty support: small drops in waist, cholesterol in overweight adults, and blood pressure in type 2 diabetes.

sources.citation: Semba RD, et al. Resveratrol levels and all-cause mortality in older community-dwelling adults. JAMA Intern Med. 2014;174(7):1077-84.
sources.finding: Dietary resveratrol levels were not linked to death, inflammation, heart disease or cancer over nine years.
sources.population: 783 adults aged 65 and over in Chianti, Italy

sources.citation: Leisegang K, Finelli R, Sikka SC, Panner Selvam MK. Eurycoma longifolia (Jack) improves serum total testosterone in men: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials. Medicina. 2022;58(8):1047.
sources.finding: Five RCTs (232 men) showed higher total testosterone, clearest in men with low levels. Seven of nine studies used one commercial extract, Physta.
sources.population: Healthy men and men with low testosterone

sources.citation: Nair KS, et al. DHEA in elderly women and DHEA or testosterone in elderly men. N Engl J Med. 2006;355(16):1647-59.
sources.finding: Two years of DHEA did not improve body composition, fitness, strength, insulin sensitivity or quality of life.

sources.citation: Elraiyah T, et al. The benefits and harms of systemic dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in postmenopausal women with normal adrenal function: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2014;99(10):3536-42.
sources.finding: Twenty-three RCTs: DHEA did not significantly improve libido, sexual function, lipids, glucose, weight or bone density. Low-certainty evidence.
sources.population: 1,188 postmenopausal women with normal adrenal function

sources.citation: He S, et al. Impact of DHEA supplementation on testosterone and estradiol levels in postmenopausal women: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Diabetol Metab Syndr. 2025;17.
sources.finding: DHEA raised testosterone and estradiol, more at 50 mg/day or above.

sources.citation: Fisher J, reviewed by Shmerling RH. DHEA supplements: are they safe? Or effective? Harvard Health Publishing. January 27, 2025.
sources.finding: Anti-aging evidence lacking. Side effects include acne and mood change. Avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver problems or PCOS; interacts with blood thinners, hormones, antidepressants.
sources.population: Consumer guidance from a medical school publisher

sources.citation: Jurgens TM, et al. Green tea for weight loss and weight maintenance in overweight or obese adults. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2012;CD008650.
sources.finding: Outside Japan, green tea preparations changed weight by 0.04 kg over 12 weeks; any loss was small and not clinically important. Japanese trials varied.
sources.population: Overweight or obese adults in 18 RCTs

sources.citation: EFSA ANS Panel. Scientific opinion on the safety of green tea catechins. EFSA J. 2018;16(4):5239.
sources.finding: Brewed green tea is generally safe. Supplements at 800 mg EGCG/day or more raised liver enzymes in trials; rare liver injury also reported with infusions.
sources.population: EU adults; interventional trials and case reports

sources.citation: Oketch-Rabah HA, et al. United States Pharmacopeia (USP) comprehensive review of the hepatotoxicity of green tea extracts. Toxicol Rep. 2020;7:386-402.
sources.finding: Liver injury case reports involved 140 to about 1,000 mg EGCG/day; taking extract fasting raises EGCG absorption. USP label: take with food, avoid with liver problems.
sources.population: Human case reports, trials and animal toxicology

sources.citation: Bulman A, D'Cunha NM, Marx W, Turner M, McKune A, Naumovski N. The effects of L-theanine consumption on sleep outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Med Rev. 2025;81:102076.
sources.finding: Pooled trials showed small gains in self-rated sleep onset, sleep quality and daytime function with L-theanine; few trials used pure L-theanine, and dose remains unsettled.
sources.population: 19 RCTs, 897 participants, all ages and health status

sources.citation: Soh J, Raventhiran S, Lee JH, Lim ZX, Goh J, Kennedy BK, Maier AB. The effect of glycine administration on the characteristics of physiological systems in human adults: a systematic review. GeroScience. 2024.
sources.finding: Glycine's most positive effects were on the nervous system; sleep gains in healthy adults came from small studies with high risk of bias.
sources.population: Human adult glycine studies across eleven physiological systems

sources.citation: Bannai M, Kawai N, Ono K, Nakahara K, Murakami N. The effects of glycine on subjective daytime performance in partially sleep-restricted healthy volunteers. Front Neurol. 2012;3:61.
sources.finding: After shortened sleep, 3 g glycine at bedtime eased day-one fatigue and sped vigilance reaction time; most other measures unchanged. Seven analysed, all Ajinomoto employees.
sources.population: 7 healthy Japanese men aged 30-61, single-blind crossover

sources.citation: Barforoush F, Ebrahimi S, Karimian Abdar M, Khademi S, Morshedzadeh N. The effect of tart cherry on sleep quality and sleep disorders: a systematic review. Food Sci Nutr. 2025;13(9):e70923.
sources.finding: Of seven tart cherry studies, three found better sleep measures and three higher melatonin; doses, durations and groups varied widely, so evidence is limited.
sources.population: 7 interventional studies in mixed adult groups

sources.citation: Howatson G, Bell PG, Tallent J, Middleton B, McHugh MP, Ellis J. Effect of tart cherry juice (Prunus cerasus) on melatonin levels and enhanced sleep quality. Eur J Nutr. 2012.
sources.finding: Seven days of tart cherry concentrate raised urinary melatonin and lengthened total sleep and sleep efficiency versus placebo.

sources.citation: Losso JN, Finley JW, Karki N, Liu AG, Prudente A, Tipton R, Yu Y, Greenway FL. Pilot study of the tart cherry juice for the treatment of insomnia and investigation of mechanisms. Am J Ther. 2018.
sources.finding: 240 ml tart cherry juice twice daily for two weeks added about 84 minutes of measured sleep versus placebo, in eight completers.
sources.population: Adults over 50 with insomnia, placebo crossover, 8 completers
